newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-FREEMAN BECOMES FIRST ABORIGINAL TO WIN WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FREEMAN BECOMES FIRST ABORIGINAL TO WIN WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Australian Cathy Freeman made a special mark in the history of her sport on Monday when she became the first Aboriginal to win a world title.
Freeman, second at last year's Atlanta Olympics, fended off a late challenge from Jamaican Sandie Richards and American Jearl Miles-Clark to win the women's 400 metres from lane one in 49.77 seconds.
Five years ago, Freeman became the first Aboriginal to compete at an Olympics when she ran in Barcelona.
On Monday, she celebrated her historic victory by carrying both the Aboriginal and Australian flags around the track.

After securing only the second world gold medal for her country after Rob de Castella's marathon title at the 1983 Helsinki championships, Freeman said she had been under pressure knowing she had a chance to enter the history books.
"I did it despite the lane and the outside pressure," she said. "I did not have a lot of energy at the end. But even if I had had just a tiny bit of energy I was going to carry both flags.
"The medal I won at the Olympics made little children realise that they had got a chance.
"I take my role model very seriously...I have never really had a horrible experience of racial discrimination. (But) history, the way my ancestors were treated, is what I have gained strength from."
Freeman jumped up and down on the podium in delight with a huge smile on her face before she was presented with her medal and she was close to tears when the Australian national anthem was played.
Her rivals were quick to praise her achievement.
"It is very important for her because there is still a lot of prejudice in Australia against Cathy," said silver medallist Richards. "She is trying to ride above it."
Freeman said she had had problems motivating herself in the season after the Olympics.

"My over-riding emotion now is relief. I want to savour the moment," she said. "There have been times when I have been pretty down. It was not until I came to Europe in June that I got my passion again."
